questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
opportunities to explore nature and outdoor life in the area
a good student enviorment

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The exchange in it self was great, but all the work surronding aplicattions, pre-aproval of subjects and so on have been exhausting and complicated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction meeting on zoom, which was helpful but after that you were pretty much on your own.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recived very little assitance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
it was very easy through Sammen, but the rooms are of very variyng quality and most places are not very social. You might be better off finding private housing through
hybel.no
or
finn.no
.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I dont think there is any "on campus" housing, but many of the Sammen housing are close to the campuses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different deadlines and webpages to keep track off. There are both open and restricted course plus language course, that require seperated registration. You can find the courses and deadlines on the UiB website, but the registration needs to be done through another system called studentweb. You can change your course on studentweb as well if there are still free spots and the courses are open. rember to check course schedule and exams dates are compatible when registrating for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you are already in Bergen you can vistit the Student Information Centre. If not you can write and email to the International Centre UiB.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to registre for most of the course I wanted, but some of them had lectures at the same time, so I was not able to follow both courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for many courses as the schedule for lectures and exams dates are published quite late, and might be at the same time, so you might not be able to follow all the courses that you want and will need a backup. (most important if you want to follow restricted courses)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were very little interactive teaching/lab work/exercises

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses i took in Bergen was lower than what I have been used too at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were very little interactive teaching/lab work/exercises compared to what I am used to at UCPH, which was a bit dissapointing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Tumor biology 
Cellular and molecular neurosceince
UN sustainable development goal 15: life on land

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: UN sustainable development goal 15: life on land was a very intresting course, I felt like I learned a lot about different aspects of sustanability. the course has a lot of group work so its also a nice way to meet other students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bergen students sports association (BSI) offer a lot of different sports activities.
Sammen offer a range of course and social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BSI Friluft have a lot of fun and social activites including climbing, bone fires and social gatherings as well as weekend trips to the mountains. Its a great way to explore the norwegian nature and get to know a lot of nice people at the same time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skiiing trips or hiking trips to the DNT cabins are great and very accessible from Bergen

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as the norwegian culture is not to different from the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Joining the student culture house "kvarteret" as a volunteer.
Joining a BSI sport

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any of the differences particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The accessible to nature and outdoor activities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. participate in as many activites you can, espaccially in the start of your stay 
2. Even though there is a lot of paper work and thinks to take care of, it is al worth it in the end. 
3. Rember to enjoy your time on exchange, 5 months passes by very quickly!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: as an exchange student it is possible to take courses from several faculties and as a native danish speaker it is possible to take course in norwegian as well as english.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Expercing a different culture, meeting new people, learning a new languages, seeing new places.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being away from friends and family for such a long time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
